channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Raheim Sanders (hip) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 12 game against the Raiders.
item.description: Todd Monken said he’s “hoping” to activate Sanders, who has only gotten in limited practices this week. He sounds truly questionable for Sunday Night Football. If active, Sanders will cut into Dylan Sampson’s backup workload a bit.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Browns signed LS Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.
item.description: Sunahara, 30 years young, has been the Browns’ snapper of balls that go longer than the league average since 2024. He’s now inked through his age-34 season.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Abdul Carter (calf/illness) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Colts.
item.description: Carter is also no longer listed with an ankle injury, which is a good sign. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) is also cleared to face a Colts offense now led by Anthony Richardson.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 12 against the Colts.
item.description: Likely injured his groin last Friday and caught one pass for 35 yards two days later. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full today, which is encouraging. Likely is a TE1 for Week 12 against the Colts.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Carlton Davis (knee) won’t play in New England’s Week 12 game against the Chargers.
item.description: He didn’t practice at all this week and doesn’t seem especially close to playing at this point. Davis has not played since Week 9. The Patriots are having enough trouble struggling with the maximum number of IR-return slots that Drake Maye hasn’t been placed on IR either, so we won’t slag them for Davis not being there, but he doesn’t look close.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Rams signed TE Jack Stoll off San Francisco’s practice squad.
item.description: With both Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee week-to-week, the Rams have brought in reinforcements behind Colby Parkinson and Max Klare. There’s no need to project Stoll to real fantasy work, but he could find some playing time if they continue to play 13-personnel sets.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on Washington’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description: A rough Cardinals defense could get Burks into the deep league conversation, but he’s had just six targets in two games since returning from the bye week. If he doesn’t do something this week, Brandon Aiyuk might be knocking on the door of his starting spot come Week 13.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on the Jaguars’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
item.description: Meyers will expectedly function as the Jaguars’ No. 1 wide receiver with Parker Washington (shoulder) sidelined and considered week-to-week. Meyers accordingly vaults into the WR2/3 range and could deliver a big stat line against a soft Titans defense.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rashod Bateman (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description: You know what you’re getting into if you start Bateman, but he did manage a touchdown grab against the Panthers last week and the Ravens have generally pumped up their passing usage since Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore. He’s probably a bit below the FLEX line in standard leagues, but it wouldn’t shock us if he landed in that area this week against the Texans.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Jaguars ruled out Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) for Week 12 against the Titans.
item.description: Chris Rodriguez should be added wherever he is available. Tuten will finally take a week off after playing through foot and ankle injuries for multiple weeks. He reportedly aggravated the issues in Week 11 against the Giants. Hopefully, Tuten will return for the Jaguars’ expectedly fantasy-friendly game against the Bears in Week 13.-Nic Bodiford
